solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tennis match is repeated on compound

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: a compound is something mixed from several parts
something that is repeated doubles

explanation.surface: A tennis fixture keeps being replayed on some walled compound.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the tennis event in which each side is a pair made up of a man and a woman.

clue.text: Characters that lean, showing stress

definitions.meaning: letters set in a sloping typeface
sloping type is the usual way to mark emphasis in print

explanation.definitionFit: Sloping print is both a style of lettering and the standard device for marking emphasis on a word.

clue.text: Lots to enter recording Sandy's disheartening medical condition

indicators.note: one piece is to go inside the other, so the record is entered by the heap

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
a pile of something is lots of it

indicators.note: taking the heart out of the word leaves only its outside letters

explanation.surface: A dispiriting illness affects Sandy after heaps of records go in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sandy's' with its middle removed leaves S and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A neurological disorder marked by recurring seizures is a long-recognised medical condition.

clue.text: Stupid name, admits head of marketing

indicators.note: the naming word lets another letter in, taking it inside itself

parts.note: to dub someone is to give them a name

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A foolish brand name lets the marketing chief in.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, especially in American English, a dumb person is a stupid one.

clue.text: Perhaps dirty appearance evident in a French claret

indicators.note: the appearance is seen inside the French article

parts.note: une is the French feminine word for a
putting in an appearance is making a show
claret is a dark red colour, named after the wine

explanation.surface: Something seen in a French red wine looks a bit grubby.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has skipped their wash may well be grimy; 'perhaps' marks the link as only likely.

clue.text: European city, centre of excellence in fabrication

indicators.note: the middle letters are put inside the untruth

parts.note: a fabrication is a lie

indicators.note: the centre of a ten-letter word is its two middle letters

explanation.surface: A Continental city is hailed as a hub of excellence in manufacturing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excellence' has ten letters, so its centre is the pair LL.
explanation.definitionFit: Lille is a large city in northern France, near the Belgian border.

clue.text: Upstairs, a rug's caught in the legs

indicators.note: the reversed letters close around a further little word, catching it
in a down clue going upstairs means the letters run upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: a rug is a mat; a mat's gives the letters with S

explanation.surface: Climbing the stairs, someone gets their legs tangled in a rug.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse or a story that has legs has the staying power to keep going.

clue.text: Naval officer bearing defeat

parts.note: a quarter is a compass bearing, one of the four directions
to master an opponent is to defeat them

explanation.surface: A naval officer's bearing amounts to defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: In the navy this is the petty officer responsible for steering and signals, a recognised naval rank.

clue.text: Tree unknown, first leaving mild confusion

parts.note: bamboo is a tall woody plant loosely called a tree
z is a mathematical unknown

indicators.note: the first letter of the mild word goes

parts.note: clement weather is mild

explanation.surface: With a tree unidentified and the earliest one gone, there is a little puzzlement.
explanation.definitionFit: To be bamboozled is to be baffled, so this noun is a state of bafflement.

clue.text: Posh auntie regularly in company of peculiar element

parts.note: U is the classic label for upper-class usage

indicators.note: the picked letters go inside the odd word

parts.note: rum is old British slang for peculiar

indicators.note: taking every other letter of the word

explanation.surface: A grand aunt keeps strange company with an odd element.
explanation.walkthrough: Alternate letters of 'auntie' are A, N, I; they go inside RUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A radioactive metal, atomic number 92, is a chemical element.

clue.text: Articles on lust involved mistress abroad

indicators.note: in an across clue a piece placed on another follows it
letters that are involved are tangled up, so rearranged

parts.note: an and a are both indefinite articles

explanation.surface: Reports about desire implicate a foreign lover.
explanation.definitionFit: A sultan's wife or consort, in an Eastern court, is a foreign mistress of sorts.

clue.text: Noisily demolish hoist

indicators.note: spoken out loud, the word sounds like another

parts.note: to raze a building is to demolish it

explanation.surface: A demolition crew loudly bring something down while lifting gear works.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoist something is to lift it up, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Retired British middle-distance runner belonging to section of body

indicators.note: retired means gone back, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: a miler runs the mile, a middle-distance event
of expresses belonging, as in friend of mine

explanation.surface: A retired British miler belongs to some running club section.
explanation.definitionFit: A front leg or arm of an animal is a limb, a part of its body.

clue.text: Native American to restrain upset dog, advancing slowly

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people
to pin someone is to hold them down

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned over, so read backwards

parts.note: a pug is a small breed of dog

explanation.surface: A Native American restrains an upset dog that is stealing forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Something approaching gradually and stealthily is moving forward by slow degrees.

clue.text: Yankee's large plant in the Orient offers financial security

indicators.note: the pieces sit inside the word for the Orient

parts.note: the Orient is the East
Yankee is Y in the radio alphabet; with the possessive it gives Y and S
a tree is a large plant

explanation.surface: An American's big plantation out East gives money security.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on this idiomatic road means living in comfort, free of money worries.

clue.text: Wooden border finally completed with difficulty

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word

parts.note: with much ado means with fuss or difficulty

explanation.surface: A wooden border is at last finished, though not easily.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the lower part of a room's wall, often panelled in wood, forming a border.

clue.text: Snake stifles source of trouble, aquatic bird in south Africa

indicators.note: the snake wraps around and smothers the other pieces

parts.note: a boa is a large constricting snake

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a swan is a water bird

explanation.surface: A snake smothering a water bird causes trouble in southern Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as 'a land in south Africa'.
explanation.definitionFit: Botswana is a landlocked country lying in southern Africa.

clue.text: Fertiliser left on soil

indicators.note: in an across clue a piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: to soil something is to mar or spoil it

explanation.surface: Fertiliser was left lying on the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: This lime-rich clay has long been spread on fields to enrich the earth.

clue.text: Eradicate bounder who trades aggressively

parts.note: a kangaroo bounds, and roo is its short form
a tout pushes tickets or goods on people

explanation.surface: Get rid of the cad who sells with pushy tactics.
explanation.definitionFit: To eradicate something is to dig it out completely, roots and all.

clue.text: Official day one enters porridge?

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the breakfast word

parts.note: porridge is an example of a cereal, hence the question mark
Mon is the usual short form of Monday
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: On some official occasion one person dips into the porridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal ritual occasion is an official one, so the adjective fits.

clue.text: At home, bones put in cooking fat, turning on the back burner

parts.note: to be in is to be at home

indicators.note: the doctor's letters go inside the reversed oil
turning round means the word is read backwards

parts.note: oil is used as cooking fat
Bones, from sawbones, is slang for a doctor, and MB is a medical degree

explanation.surface: At home, bones go into the frying fat while dinner waits on a back ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bones' looks like skeleton parts but is the doctor nickname (from sawbones); 'turning' gives LIO, which 'put in' opens for the medical degree letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left in suspension, awaiting a decision, has been put aside for later.

clue.text: Occasional trailer one's seen among produce being brought back

indicators.note: the pieces are seen inside the reversed produce
brought back means turned round, so read backwards

parts.note: crops are farm produce
a trailer is an advertisement for a film, an ad
I is the Roman numeral one; the 's is the verb is

explanation.surface: A film trailer appears among farm goods carted back home now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produce' looks like a verb but is the farm noun; 'being brought back' gives SPORC, with the advert and Roman one 'seen among' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sporadic happens irregularly, now and then, which is what occasional means.

clue.text: The German's covered in gold for farewell

indicators.note: the German word sits inside the gold symbol

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
die is a German word for the; the 's is the verb is

explanation.surface: The German is draped in gold for a goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: Borrowed from French, this is a goodbye, used as a word of farewell.

clue.text: Proposal emerged to ring-fence American capital

indicators.note: the words fence in the answer, which sits within them

explanation.surface: A plan surfaced to ring-fence US funds.
explanation.definitionFit: Salem is the state capital of Oregon, an American capital city.

clue.text: Correct time showed up

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the letters run backwards

parts.note: tide is an old word for time, as in Eastertide

explanation.surface: The right time duly appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit a text is to correct and revise it.

clue.text: Dicky ignored eating away

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for faulty or shaky, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone with a dodgy heart was ignored as their strength wasted away.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearing something down gradually is eating it away, as water does to rock.

clue.text: In Scotland, they carry heavy fish miles into hideaway

indicators.note: the pieces go into the hiding place

parts.note: a den is a hideaway or lair
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: Scots carrying heavy fish trek miles to a hideout.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scotland, heavy is a type of beer, so the definition means the men who deliver beer barrels.
explanation.definitionFit: Brewery deliverymen traditionally hauled barrels of beer on a horse-drawn cart.

clue.text: Musician and tenor drink with beloved prime minister earlier

parts.note: rum is a drink
a pet is a beloved favourite
John Major was a British prime minister in the 1990s

explanation.surface: A singer has a drink with a darling former premier.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a cavalry rank for the chief bandsman, a military musician.
